99	    it always has. This is the identity wrapper so the toy race is unchanged.

104	    def to(self, device):                      # call sites do tx.to(device)

600	## 4. `_progressive_eval_freq` — bound total evals to ~250-500 over 20 000 steps
601	
602	### 4.1 The arithmetic
603	
604	`early_stop_max_steps = 20_000` (`:264`). A fixed `eval_every` of `E` ⇒ `20000/E` evals:
605	
606	| target evals | fixed `eval_every` |
607	|---|---|
608	| 500 | 40 |
609	| 250 | 80 |
610	| ~333 | 60 |
611	
612	So a **plain fixed `eval_every≈50-80`** already lands in band. But the existing
613	`_progressive_eval_freq` is *sigmoid-increasing* (evals MORE often later) — at scale we
614	want the opposite emphasis (cheap early, but never sub-40). Retune so the **integral over
615	[1,20000]** sits in [250,500].
616	
617	### 4.2 Retuned signature
618	
619	```python
620	def _progressive_eval_freq(step, base_freq=40, max_freq=200, scale=0.0005, thresh=8000):
621	    """Eval-interval schedule for the SCALED regime: eval sparsely early (interval
622	    ~max_freq), tighten toward base_freq as training matures. Returns the STEP
623	    INTERVAL between evals (NOT a rate). Tuned so total evals over a 20k-step
624	    budget land in ~[250,500]:
625	        early interval ≈ max_freq (200) → cheap;
626	        late  interval ≈ base_freq (40)  → resolve grok/plateau finely;
627	        crossover at `thresh` (8000).
628	    Integral of 1/interval over [1,20000] ≈ 300 evals (verified §4.3)."""
629	    heat = 1.0 / (1.0 + math.exp(-scale * (step - thresh)))   # 0 early → 1 late
630	    interval = max_freq - (max_freq - base_freq) * heat        # 200 → 40

150	### 2.2 Streaming source (single pass)
151	Two interchangeable sources, both yielding a flat uint16 token stream:
152	
153	* **HF streaming** (`streaming=True`): `load_dataset("HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu",
154	  name="sample-10BT", split="train", streaming=True)`, iterate `ex["text"]`,
155	  BPE-encode, append `eot` (50256) between docs. Single forward pass; never
156	  re-iterated.
157	* **Local sample-10BT** (~27GB on `/workspace`): if a pre-tokenized
158	  `*.bin` (uint16) shard dir is present (config `fineweb_bin_dir`), `np.memmap`
159	  each shard read-only and walk linearly. This avoids re-tokenizing every run and
160	  is the CPU-only-friendly path (HF streaming + BPE on CPU is slow; memmap is the
161	  default when the bin dir exists).
162	
163	Determinism: the **stream order is fixed** (HF streaming is deterministic for a
164	fixed dataset revision; memmap walk is index-order). Per-step batch sampling uses
165	a **seeded** `np.random.Generator(np.random.PCG64(seed))` over a rolling window,
166	so A/A/A reproduces bit-identically given the same seed + same source bytes. The
167	config pins `fineweb_revision` (a dataset commit hash) so the corpus is frozen.
168	
169	### 2.3 Rolling buffer (a few GB)
170	A ring buffer of uint16 tokens, capacity `buf_tokens` (config; default 1<<30 ≈
171	1.07B tokens ≈ 2.1 GB at 2 bytes/token). A background-free, synchronous refill:
172	when the consumed cursor passes a low-water mark, pull more from the source and
173	overwrite the oldest region. Batches are sampled as random `[B]` start offsets
174	within the *currently-resident* window, each of length `T+1` (T inputs +
175	1 shifted target per position). This gives an i.i.d.-ish stream of contiguous
176	chunks without holding the whole corpus.
177	
178	CPU-only note: the buffer is a host `np.uint16` array; per-step we slice B×(T+1),
179	build `tokens int32 [B,T]` and `targets int32 [B,T]`, move to device. No GPU
180	memory blow-up (only the live batch is on-device).
181	
182	### 2.4 Fixed eval probe (sampled ONCE)
183	At load, BEFORE the train stream advances, read the FIRST `probe_tokens` tokens
184	(config; default 8M) from the source into a frozen contiguous uint16 array
185	`eval_probe`. This is reshaped into `[n_probe, T]` non-overlapping windows. Every
186	eval forwards exactly this same array (optionally in fixed sub-batches), so eval
187	is identical every time and the full split is NEVER iterated. The probe tokens
188	are then SKIPPED for training (the train stream starts after the probe region) so
189	train/eval don't overlap — a clean held-out probe from the single pass.
190	
191	### 2.5 Per-position causal-LM CE
192	For a `[B,T]` token window, targets are the same window shifted by 1:
193	`targets[b,t] = tokens[b,t+1]`. CE is averaged over all `B*T` positions. This is
194	the standard next-token objective. (On Layer A's vocab-99/seq-4 smoke, this is
195	computed eagerly in the probe-eval path; on the real Layer-B kernel it is the
196	kernel's loss — see §4 coupling.)

200	batch and calls `fused_train_step` exactly as today — `tokens int32 [B,T]`,

339	class _MemmapSource:
340	    def __init__(self, shards):
341	        self.mm = [_np.memmap(s, dtype=_np.uint16, mode="r") for s in shards]

347	        while got < n and self.shard < len(self.mm):

349	            out[got:got+take] = m[self.pos:self.pos+take]; got += take
350	            self.pos += take

359	            self.pos += take; rem -= take

475	def _eval_log_fineweb(r, step, m, probe, c, st, pb):

487	    pb.set_postfix({"ce":f"{val_ce:.3f}","acc":f"{val_acc:.3f}"}, refresh=False)

39	### 1.1 Model-size coupling — FLAG, do NOT change model defs
40	
41	ImageNet is 224×224 RGB, patch16 ⇒ **196 patches** (14×14 grid), **patch_dim = 16·16·3 = 768**, **1000 classes**. The current ViT defaults are `patch_dim=49 / num_patches=16 / classes=p=97`. These three are *all* config keys (`_raw_model` :503, `out=Linear(d,p)` :423). So the resize is done **entirely via config**, with NO edit to the `ViT` class:
42	
43	| key | MNIST-add value | ImageNet-1k value | source of truth |
44	|---|---|---|---|
45	| `p` (= classifier head width & `logits[:, :p]` slice) | 97 | **1000** | `out=Linear(d,p)` :423; `evaluate` slice :539; `_eval_log` slice :746 |
46	| `patch_dim` | 49 | **768** (16·16·3) | `patch_proj=Linear(patch_dim,d)` :419 |
47	| `num_patches` | 16 | **196** ((224/16)²) | `pos=Embedding(num_patches+1,d)` :421; `pos_ids` :424 |
48	
49	**This is a model-size coupling, flagged per the task.** Consequences the lead must accept:
50	- The ViT param count changes: `patch_proj` grows `49·d → 768·d`, `pos` grows `17·d → 197·d`, `out` grows `d·97 → d·1000`. For the toy `d=128` race this is still tiny (~0.5 M → ~1.3 M params). For the **flagship `vit` d=1664/L48** (`MODEL_SCALES_BY_MODEL["flagship"]["vit"]` :252) it is the canonical ViT-G/14-ish patch16/224 footprint.
51	- **The L3-TC ViT megakernel is hard-pinned to patch_dim=49 / num_patches=16 / 97-class / 32-tensor / 418017-param layout** (`INTEGRATION-VIT.md` §0–§1: `vit_layout.cuh` `static_assert`s on count=32 / total=418017 / smem budget; oracle `vit_param_layout()`). **Changing `patch_dim`/`num_patches`/`p` BREAKS that fused cell's static layout — the megakernel will refuse (or mis-compute) at the new shapes.** Per PROJECT TRUTH (L3-TC persistent wgmma megakernel only; `_record_train_path`/`_try_fused_train_step` HARD-RAISE rather than silently fall back, :794, dispatch.cpp "no silent fallback"), an ImageNet-shaped ViT will **HARD-RAISE inside `_try_fused_train_step`** unless/until a sibling regenerates a `vit_imagenet` cell at the new layout. **This is a separate kernel-codegen task and OUT OF SCOPE for this data-wiring draft.** I document it as the gating risk; the data path below is correct regardless, and is independently exercisable via the eager reference (e.g. an `imagenet` smoke that asserts shapes only, or once the lead wires a non-fused validation harness). **I do not modify any kernel / layout / dispatch file.**

53	So: **no edit to `ViT`, `EncoderBlock`, `_raw_model`, `build_model`, `evaluate`, `_eval_log`, the train loops, or any `csrc/` file.** The cell is configured purely by setting `p=1000, patch_dim=768, num_patches=196, model_type="vit"` in the config that reaches `run_pipeline`/`make_data_for_task`, plus the new data branch below.

55	### 1.2 Patchify must match the ViT's flatten convention
56	
57	The ViT does `patch_proj(x)` where `x` is `[B, num_patches, patch_dim]`, then prepends CLS and adds `pos(arange(num_patches+1))`. So the data builder owns: (a) row-major patch ordering (patch index = `row*14 + col`, must be stable across train/probe), (b) the in-patch flatten of the 16×16×3 block to a length-768 vector. I mirror the existing MNIST builder's `unfold(...).reshape(...)` idiom (:341) but for 3 channels. **Convention pinned (documented in code):** patch grid row-major; in-patch flatten = `(C, ph, pw) → reshape(768)` with C-outermost (channel, then patch-row, then patch-col). The ViT is permutation-equivariant over patch *features* only through a single Linear, so any FIXED bijection works **as long as train and probe use the identical one** — I use one shared `_patchify_chw()` helper so they cannot diverge.
58	
59	### 1.3 Streaming train, fixed probe eval — the two-tensor split
60	
61	Because the harness is whole-tensor full-batch, I cannot hand `make_data_for_task` a 1.28 M-sample train tensor. Two sub-decisions:
62	
63	**(A) Train: a streamed, pre-augmented batch flow folded into a finite on-device "train view".**
64	The cleanest minimal-diff move that keeps the existing full-batch train loops *unmodified* is: the ImageNet branch returns a **fixed-size train tensor that is a once-sampled, pre-augmented slice of the stream** sized to the step budget, NOT the whole 1.28 M. Concretely, `make_data_for_task` returns `x_train [B_train, 196, 768]` where `B_train = c["imagenet_train_view"]` (default 8192 — a "<1 epoch re-see" budget, owner-sanctioned). The train loops then full-batch over this view exactly as today. This is faithful to "budget re-sees <1 epoch so safe": the view is sampled once from the stream with standard random aug, and the run never completes an epoch, so re-seeing the same augmented view across steps is the intended (grokking-style) regime. (If the lead later wants true per-step fresh batches, that is a train-loop change — a separate task; this draft keeps train-loop diffs at ZERO.)
65	
66	**(B) Eval probe: ONE fixed 50k-subset tensor, sampled once, reused every eval.**
67	The task pins this: "FIXED held-out probe = the standard 50k val subset sampled once, reused every eval (cap eval to seconds)." I sample `n_probe = c["imagenet_probe_n"]` (default **2048**) deterministically (seed-fixed) from the **standard ImageNet val split** (the canonical 50k), apply **eval transform only** (resize-256 → center-crop-224, no random aug), patchify, and materialize ONE `[n_probe, 196, 768]` fp32 tensor. This becomes BOTH `x_val`/`x_test` returned to the harness, so the existing `_eval_log` whole-tensor forward of `vax`/`tex` runs unchanged and finishes in <~1 s for 2048 samples on GPU (and is the early-stop trigger's input via `va`). 2048 ≪ 50k keeps eval in "seconds"; the subset is itself sampled once from the 50k and cached on disk so it is byte-identical every eval and across runs/seeds (the "sampled once, reused" requirement). `n_probe` is configurable up to the full 50k if the lead wants a tighter estimate and can afford the eval cost.
68	
69	> Why val==test here: the harness 6-tuple has separate val/test, and `_eval_log` reports both. ImageNet has one held-out set (the 50k val); there is no separate labelled test. I return the **same** fixed probe tensor for both slots so `val_acc` (the early-stop trigger, `early_stop_on="val"`) and the reported `test_acc` are the identical, honest top-1-on-held-out number. The train-view is disjoint from the probe by construction (probe is drawn from the val split, train-view from the train split), so there is no train/eval leakage. **Documented in code.**

73	`EarlyStopper` (:542) stops when the criterion acc `>= threshold` held for `patience` evals. 30	**Implication (this is the central design decision, documented per the task):**
31	GiftEval is real-valued forecasting (context window → horizon H, MSE/MAE or
32	CRPS/quantile). The Mamba cell physically **cannot** ingest floats or emit a
33	regression scalar without (a) editing `Mamba3Model.forward` / the head, (b) editing
34	`evaluate`/`_eval_log`, and (c) recompiling the megakernel with different `constexpr`
35	dims — **all three are forbidden** by PROJECT TRUTH (model defs unchanged; megakernel

38	So the wiring casts forecasting into the **existing classification ABL** by
39	**discretizing the series into a vocabulary of 97 bins** and framing the task as
40	*"next-step bin classification"*: the model reads a length-8 context window of
41	quantized values (token ids in `[0,96]`, with `97`/`98` as separator/pad to fill the
42	`vocab=99` budget exactly like the mod-97 task uses `op_tok=97`,`eq_tok=98`) and
43	predicts the **bin of the next value** (a 97-way class). This is the
44	*classification-by-binning* framing standard in TSFMs that quantize (Chronos-style
45	tokenization): a forecast over a fixed quantile grid is exactly a categorical
46	distribution over bins, which gives us **both**:
47	
48	* **point** metric → de-quantize argmax bin to its bin-center → MAE/MASE;
49	* **probabilistic** metric → the 97-way softmax over bin-centers **is** a discrete
50	  predictive distribution → CRPS directly (no separate quantile head needed).
51	
52	This is the **only** framing that reuses the frozen `[B,8] long → 97-class` ABI with
53	**zero** model-def, eval, or megakernel changes. The coupling to `seq=8` / `d=128` is
54	real and is **documented, not changed** (§6).

56	**Note on horizon.** The frozen ABI emits **one** class (last-token, 97-way). A
57	multi-step horizon `H>1` would need either H heads (head change — forbidden) or
58	autoregressive rollout (an inference-loop change to `evaluate`, which currently
59	forwards the WHOLE tensor in one shot, `:537`). The minimal-diff draft therefore

62	which is a sidecar that never touches `evaluate`. H is a config knob

124	## 2. Quantization (series → token ids in the frozen vocab)
125	
126	The whole framing hinges on a **fixed, global, reproducible** value→bin map. We use a
127	**per-series mean-scaled, global-quantile** binning (Chronos-style), computed ONCE on
128	the sampled training series and frozen into the manifest:
129	
130	1. **Scale** each series by its own context mean-abs (`s_i = mean(|x_ctx|)+eps`),
131	   i.e. `z = x / s_i`. This is the MASE/CRPS normalizer too (kept for de-norm).
132	2. **Bin edges:** `P = 97` bins. Edges are the 96 inner quantiles of the *pooled
133	   scaled* training values, computed once over the sampled corpus, clamped to a
134	   symmetric range `[-q_hi, q_hi]` (default 99.5th pct), stored in the manifest as
135	   `bin_edges:[96]` and `bin_centers:[97]`. Reused verbatim every eval (no re-fit).
136	3. **Encode:** `tok = digitize(z, bin_edges)  ∈ [0,96]`.  Separator token `97`, pad
137	   `98` (mirrors `op_tok=p`, `eq_tok=p+1` in `make_data`). Vocab budget = 99 exactly.
138	4. **Decode (point):** `x_hat = bin_centers[argmax_class] * s_i`.
139	5. **Decode (prob):** predictive pmf = `softmax(logits[:,:97])` over `bin_centers*s_i`
140	   → a discrete distribution → CRPS in original units.
141	
142	The `bin_edges`/`bin_centers`/quantization params live in the **manifest**, NOT in
143	model defs — they are pure data, satisfying "don't change model defs."

341	## 4. Fixed held-out window probe (sampled ONCE, reused every eval)
342	
343	The task demands a **fixed** held-out window set, sampled once, reused every eval, on
344	which we report **normalized MASE / CRPS** — and **never** iterate the full corpus.
345	
346	This is a **sidecar** (`gifteval_probe.py`): it does **not** touch `evaluate`/
347	`_eval_log`/`EarlyStopper` (those keep classification acc for the grok criterion). The
348	probe is called explicitly at finalize (a one-line hook in `_fin`, §5) or run
349	standalone post-hoc against a checkpoint.
350	
351	### 4.1 Why a separate metric from the early-stop criterion
352	
353	`EarlyStopper` (`:558`) and `_eval_log` (`:744-746`) are classification-acc machinery
354	and are LOAD-BEARING for the grok gate and the megakernel wiring guard. We leave them
355	**exactly** as-is (the grok criterion becomes "next-bin top-1 acc ≥ 0.95"). MASE/CRPS
356	are *reporting* metrics computed by the probe, decoupled from early-stop. This keeps
357	A/A/A determinism and the fp64 gate on the unchanged forward.

376	    if PROBE_CACHE.exists():

409	    """Forecast on the FIXED windows. Point: argmax-bin -> center*scale -> MASE.
410	    Prob: softmax-over-centers -> CRPS (closed form on the discrete pmf). H-step via
